meta.title: Private-equity competitive landscape for Broad Sky Partners (LMM business & consumer services)
meta.method: Started from the must-cover candidate list plus sponsors found while tracing who owns the consolidators active in each BSP platform's niche (residential HVAC/plumbing/electrical in PA/NJ, electrical/energy contracting, legal managed services, lab supply distribution, public affairs, consumer brands). Pulled facts from firm websites and press releases (fund closes, portfolio pages, news archives), newswire/trade coverage, and deal trackers (PrivSource, DealSeam, Cascade Partners' H2-2025 electrical M&A report, Copper Run). Each firm was checked for fit and dropped if its mandate did not overlap BSP. Threat levels are analyst judgments combining equity-check overlap with BSP's $50-250M range, sector overlap with named BSP platforms, and geographic overlap (Central PA/NJ, New England).
sources_summary: Firm websites & press releases (midoceanpartners.com, alpineinvestors.com, gryphon-inv.com, sterlinglp.com, knoxlane.com, gridironcapital.com, truarcpartners.com, watchtowercp.com, kohlberg.com, stonecalibre.com, stonepoint.com, eagletree.com, vesterracap.com, courtsquare.com, etc.)
PR Newswire / Business Wire / GlobeNewswire release pages (some Business Wire pages returned 403 and are cited as search-result URLs)

Deal trackers: PrivSource (PA HVAC acquisitions; electrical services acquirers), DealSeam HVAC PE roll-up tracker 2026, Cascade Partners Electrical Contracting M&A Update H2 2025, Copper Run deal announcements, Tracxn/PitchBook public profile snippets
Trade/business press: LA Business Journal, LebTown, Central Penn Business Journal, PE Hub, Private Equity Wire, homepros.news, Global Legal Post, Buyouts Insider
Wikipedia (HQ/founding/fund history cross-checks for Trivest, Kohlberg, Court Square, CIVC, HCI, Leonard Green)
Broad Sky Partners team bio (Tyler Zachem prior roles at MidOcean/DB Capital Partners and Carlyle)

bsp_reference.first_exit: Smith + Howard to TPG Growth (announced 2026-06-08, closed 2026-08-06)

landscape_summary: BSP is one of the smallest institutional sponsors on this map. Fund I is about $137M, while peers competing for similar deals run $0.9-2.1B flagships (Trivest VII $950M, CIVC VII $870M, Comvest/Vesterra VI $881M, Bertram V $1.5B, Sterling V $1.6B, Gridiron V $2.1B, TruArc V $1.2B). BSP's $50-250M equity range therefore depends on co-invest and operating credibility, not blind-pool scale.

The closest thesis-level peers are firms that are pure business-services or services-plus-consumer shops in a similar equity band: MidOcean (Zachem's former firm, same sector taxonomy including franchise services and media/marketing), CIVC (business-services only; legal support, IT, utility services), Trilantic North America ($50-300M checks, business services + consumer), Palladium ($50-150M), Vesterra/Comvest (up to $150M) and Bertram ($150-500M EV).

Residential services (Punctual Pros) is the most crowded field. National consolidators (Apex/Alpine, Wrench/LGP, TurnPoint/OMERS, Redwood/Altas, Any Hour/Knox Lane, T3/Riverside) set add-on pricing. In PA/NJ specifically, Sila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy Service Partners/HL Bowman (Gridiron), Ally Services (Watchtower) and Northwinds (TruArc) are buying in or next to Punctual Pros' counties.

Commercial electrical and energy services (CET) have only recently drawn institutional money. Cascade Partners reports that PE now accounts for most electrical-contractor M&A since 2023, with new platforms from Kohlberg (RESA Power, Loenbro, plus CLEAResult in energy efficiency) and Huron (Criticore; Albireo Energy expanding into Upstate NY). CET is still one of very few sponsor-backed electrical platforms anchored in New England.

Legal services (Frontline) have a thin set of sponsor competitors: Stone Point/Aquiline's Consilio (eDiscovery/review), EagleTree's Integreon (legal managed services; ownership may have changed), CIVC's Magna Legal Services, Gridiron's Esquire Deposition Solutions, and BV Investment Partners (Frontline's former owner). None of them combines law-firm IT managed services with billing/RCM the way Frontline does.

Lab supply distribution (Thomas Scientific) has one very aggressive sponsor-backed consolidator, StoneCalibre's Calibre Scientific, which made more than a dozen lab distribution and consumables acquisitions in 2024 alone, mostly in Europe; its U.S. diagnostics foothold (Alpha-Tec) dates to 2017. Sterling's distribution mandate (consumables/MRO) is the other relevant overlap.

Public affairs and communications (BPI) turned over sponsor-to-sponsor in 2025 when Shamrock Capital bought Penta Group from Falfurrias. Most other institutional money in PR sits with large caps (KKR/FGS Global) or holding companies (Stagwell), which leaves mid-market ownership of public-affairs firms uncrowded.

Consumer apparel (Fair Harbor) has the least verified overlap in this dataset. Only generalist consumer investors (Bertram, Palladium, Trilantic, EagleTree, Gryphon) appear, and no dedicated apparel sponsor was profiled, so the competitive picture there is incomplete.

Upmarket sponsors (Leonard Green, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Court Square, Audax, Stone Point, Altas) matter mainly as exit buyers. Recent sponsor-to-sponsor trades (NEFCO Bertram to LGP, Service Logic LGP to Bain, Sila MSCP to GS, Jensen Hughes Gryphon to New Mountain, Smith + Howard BSP to TPG Growth) show deep demand for scaled services platforms.

implications_for_bsp: Punctual Pros faces the hardest add-on competition. Sila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy/HL Bowman (Gridiron) and Ally (Watchtower) are all buying in Central PA/NJ. BSP should lean on the franchise-system angle (Authority Brands territory rights, brand conversion) and on proprietary outreach to sub-$3M EBITDA shops that large-cap platforms skip, rather than join auctions.

CET has open space in New England. Institutional electrical/energy platforms (Kohlberg's RESA Power, Loenbro and CLEAResult; Huron's Criticore and Albireo) are mostly outside the six-state footprint, so CET can keep consolidating New England electrical, wastewater and energy-efficiency contractors (Horton-style) before those platforms reach the region. Albireo's Upstate NY expansion and Kohlberg's energy-efficiency cluster are the ones to watch.

Frontline's legal IT + RCM combination has no direct sponsor-backed copy. The likely challengers are Alpine's Evergreen (MSP roll-up), EagleTree/Integreon and BV (the former owner), so BSP should lock in law-firm MSP and billing-services add-ons before a generalist MSP consolidator builds a legal vertical.

Thomas Scientific should treat Calibre Scientific as its main bidding competitor for U.S. chromatography, consumables and specialty-distribution add-ons, and could use Calibre's European focus to win U.S. line-card and distribution targets.

At the fund level, MidOcean, CIVC, Trilantic NA, Palladium and Vesterra run the same business-services/consumer playbook with larger pools. The Smith + Howard exit to TPG Growth (about 100 to 800 professionals, 9 add-ons) is BSP's best proof point for Fund II fundraising and for winning founder-led deals on operating credibility. Upmarket buyers (LGP, GS, Court Square, New Mountain, Bain, TPG) are clearly paying for scaled services platforms, which supports exit multiples.

Listed as 'only if fit'; software-growth investor. Not researched further and no overlap found.
Kept as Huron Capital, but Sciens itself was sold to Carlyle in Dec 2021 and is treated as exited.

caveats: Web search quota ran out partway through research, so later firms were verified mainly from firm websites and previously retrieved search results. Some fund sizes (Gryphon VI, Trilantic VII, Palladium VI, Tailwind IV, Shore Business Services II) are unknown and set to null.
Several Business Wire pages returned HTTP 403. Where cited, those URLs come from search results rather than fetched pages.

deals_2025_2026 covers disclosed transactions only; many sponsors do not announce add-ons, so counts are lower bounds. Some entries record partial liquidity (e.g., Apollo's minority stake in Apex) or structured-equity deals typed as exit/platform with explanatory notes.
Add-on counts in platforms_relevant mix lifetime and single-year figures (see notes); treat them as indicative.
AUM figures come from different dates (e.g., Shore about $17B on its website vs. $14B+ in Oct 2025; Kohlberg about $15B in 2024 vs. $18B on its website).

HQ coordinates are city centroids (geo_precision: city). HQs for Huron (Detroit), Stone Point (Greenwich), Trilantic NA (New York), Sverica (Boston), Alpine (San Francisco) and OMERS (Toronto) come from general knowledge and were not confirmed on a fetched page.
Threat levels and implications are analyst judgments, not reported facts.
Smith + Howard is excluded as a BSP overlap sector because it was sold (TPG Growth, closed Aug 6, 2026).
Integreon: the Global Legal Post 'Law.com's owner' headline describes EagleTree's own Jun 2021 purchase (EagleTree owns ALM); no later sale found.
CIVC Fund VII ($870M, 2023) could not be confirmed on a fetched page (PitchBook blocked); civc.com confirms 7 funds and $2B invested.

items.trajectory: Founded in 2003 in New York (DB Capital Partners heritage), MidOcean grew its flagship from $1.2B (Fund V) to $1.5B+ (Fund VI, Apr 2023, ~25% larger) and has done 50+ platforms and 140+ add-ons. It broadened into alternative credit and, from 2024, structured equity (EquipmentShare, Emergency Care Partners), so not every 2025-26 deal is a control buyout. In 2026 it has mostly been harvesting business-services holdings (Questex, Zonda, SI Solutions) while keeping the same sector taxonomy that BSP's CEO helped build there.
items.threat_rationale: It uses almost the same sector map as BSP: media/marketing and professional services (BPI), infrastructure services (CET), and franchise services (Punctual Pros). Its $50-300M+ equity range overlaps BSP's $50-250M. Tyler Zachem spent 14 years at MidOcean/DB Capital Partners running Business Services, Media & Communications, so the two firms share intermediary relationships and theses. Its bigger Fund VI gives it more room on price.

items.strategy: Microcap buy-and-build investor running sector funds (healthcare, food & beverage, business services, industrials, real estate, search). The Business Services fund targets companies with $5-50M revenue and $1-7M EBITDA in IT/tech-enabled services, professional services, compliance, facility & field services and similar niches.
items.trajectory: AUM went from about $1B in 2019 to $9.1B in Oct 2024, $14B+ in Oct 2025, and about $17B on the current website. That growth came from adding sector-specific funds, including Business Services Fund II (2024) and Industrials Fund II (2026). The firm is still sub-$7M EBITDA microcap, so it mostly builds the add-on-sized companies that BSP platforms would otherwise buy.
items.threat_rationale: Shore rarely competes for BSP's $50-250M equity platform deals. It does compete for small founder-owned IT, professional and field-services companies that are natural add-ons, and at exit it sells scaled microcaps that could be BSP platforms.

items.trajectory: Alpine has raised nine flagship funds and now manages $17.7B. Fund IX hit its $4.5B hard cap in 2023, and the Apex Service Partners continuation vehicle raised $3.4B the same year. In 2025 it closed a record 190 deals (5 new platforms, from 18,000 sourced) and extended the 'Service Partners' model from home trades into windows/doors, commercial access, facility services and the UK. Selling a minority stake in Apex to Apollo in May 2026 lets Alpine hold one of the largest residential-services consolidators for longer.
items.threat_rationale: Apex is the most prolific residential HVAC/plumbing/electrical acquirer, with 130+ deals and 60 in 2025 alone, so it bids against Punctual Pros for owner-operated shops. Evergreen (IT MSP roll-up) and Medusind (RCM) overlap Frontline's service lines. Its volume-driven sourcing engine pushes up seller expectations across residential services.

items.strategy: Invests only in founder-led and family-owned businesses in the US and Canada, through four strategies: Discovery (<$4M EBITDA), Mid-Market Fund VII ($4-15M EBITDA), Growth (non-control) and Recognition (larger founder businesses). It is known for pricing certainty ('close at the price in our LOI') and has recently launched home-services platforms.
